name: TidyCal
tagline: Publish simple booking pages connected to one calendar and send confirmations

pricing.notes: Sold as a one-time AppSumo-style lifetime purchase; canonical monthly price is null.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Unlimited bookings and booking types; 1 readable calendar connection and 1 writable calendar; paid, recurring, and package bookings.

tiers.name: Individual Lifetime
tiers.limits: 10 calendar connections; group bookings; AI assistant; custom emails and analytics.

tiers.name: Agency Lifetime
tiers.limits: 25 calendar connections; unlimited team members; round-robin and collective meetings; US/Canada SMS reminders.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: 25 calendar connections; no TidyCal branding; custom domain; priority support.

pricing.freeTierCaps: Unlimited bookings and booking types; 1 readable calendar connection and 1 writable calendar; paid, recurring, and package bookings.
pricing.billingTerms: Free forever + one-time lifetime licenses + Pro monthly or annual (-31%)
pricing.hiddenCosts: Payment processing still costs extra; Agency retains reduced TidyCal branding, while complete branding removal requires Pro.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For TidyCal, publish simple booking pages connected to one calendar and send confirmations. The hard boundary is lifetime hosted service, calendar integrations, and extremely low maintenance cost, plus calendar integrations and reliability.
coreLoopDIY: Read one calendar, publish simple booking pages with availability, create conflict-safe bookings, and send confirmations and reminders.
whatYouLose: lifetime hosted service, calendar integrations, and extremely low maintenance cost
ongoingBurden: OAuth refresh, webhooks, timezone databases, race conditions, reminders, deliverability, privacy, and uptime
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for TidyCal because people pay because one double booking or missed invite can cost more than years of subscription fees. The recurring cost buys OAuth refresh, webhooks, timezone databases, race conditions, reminders, deliverability, privacy, and uptime, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Cal.com
priorArt.desc: Mature open-source scheduling platform with calendar integrations and booking workflows.

alternatives.name: Cal.com Free
alternatives.desc: Unlimited solo event types, calendars and bookings, with payments and notifications; team routing costs money.

facts.dataFormat: Account, availability, booking and integration records live in Cal.com's cloud and in the connected calendar, conferencing and payment providers
facts.gapVsPaid: It is more complex to configure, and team routing and shared scheduling remain paid even though solo use is generous.

alternatives.name: Calendly Free
alternatives.desc: One active event type and unlimited bookings; meeting polls survive, workflows and teams do not.

facts.dataFormat: Account, booking and calendar-integration records live in Calendly's cloud and connected calendar or conferencing providers
facts.gapVsPaid: The free plan allows one event type and one calendar and does not include payments or automated reminders.

alternatives.name: Google Calendar appointment schedules
alternatives.desc: One bare appointment page inside the calendar you already use; reminders, payments and polish are paid.

facts.install: Use the existing Google Calendar web app and create an appointment schedule
facts.dataFormat: Appointment schedules and resulting events live in the user's Google Account and Google Calendar
facts.gapVsPaid: The free account supplies one bare booking page without TidyCal's payment, package, recurring-booking and customization features.
facts.setupBlocker: A Google Account; creating and configuring the schedule is primarily a desktop-web workflow

alternatives.name: Koalendar Free
alternatives.desc: Unlimited booking pages and two calendar connections; payments, forms, reminders and team routing are paid.

facts.dataFormat: Account, booking and availability records live in Koalendar's cloud and connected calendar or conferencing providers
facts.gapVsPaid: Payments, form questions, custom reminders, group sessions and team scheduling are paid.

alternatives.name: YouCanBookMe Free
alternatives.desc: One booking page, but it keeps forms, payments, confirmations, polls and the calendar-overlay trick.

facts.install: Hosted signup followed by connecting a supported calendar
facts.dataFormat: Booking and account records live in YouCanBookMe's cloud, while availability is read from and events are written to the connected Google, Microsoft or Apple calendar
facts.gapVsPaid: It is limited to one booking page and one calendar and keeps YouCanBookMe branding, despite a richer form and payment feature set.
facts.setupBlocker: A supported external calendar must be connected before a booking page can work

alternatives.name: zcal Free
alternatives.desc: Unlimited links and calendars, custom questions, email reminders and Stripe payments; teams are paid and zcal takes 3%.

facts.dataFormat: Account and booking records live in zcal's cloud; Stripe processes and stores payment details for paid bookings
facts.gapVsPaid: It adds a 3% commission to Stripe payments and reserves team scheduling for paid plans.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Individual Plan plan and a single-user booking service DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for TidyCal in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, Google Calendar OAuth, and Resend; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: read one calendar, publish simple booking pages with availability, create conflict-safe bookings, and send confirmations and reminders.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Implement one account with configurable working hours, buffers, minimum notice, and booking horizon.
Connect Google Calendar using OAuth and store refresh tokens encrypted at rest.
Calculate availability in UTC and render it in the visitor's detected timezone.
Reserve slots transactionally, create calendar events, and prevent concurrent double booking.
Send confirmation, cancellation, and reminder email with signed management links.
Add an admin booking list, event-type editor, audit log, and calendar reconnect flow.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out Microsoft and Apple calendar support.
Deliberately leave out team round-robin routing.
Deliberately leave out payments, CRM workflows, and enterprise controls.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
